facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest argument that the set is ready without qualification is its recency and internal consistency: it runs to 2026-09-30, every tie-out performed agrees exactly, and compliance with all covenants is stated at each of the last four reporting dates. That is enough for a reader who needs only reported figures. It is not enough for covenant headroom, a full maturity wall or last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The eight filings and releases support a credit snapshot of Orion Group Holdings Inc as of 2026-11-18, but only on reported figures: no executed credit agreement is supplied, so covenant headroom, guarantor names and debt amortisation are not established for creditors.

The evidence runs from the 2024 annual report to the third-quarter 2026 report signed on 2026-10-28 and covers both the December 2025 refinancing and the February 2026 acquisition of J.E. McAmis. Reported debt, liquidity and covenant levels can be read directly. Leverage and coverage on the company's adjusted EBITDA need a full-year 2025 reconciliation that none of the documents contains.

### Key findings

The documents form a continuous record for one reporting entity, Orion Group Holdings, Inc. and its subsidiaries, from the 2022 fiscal year to the nine months to 2026-09-30, and nothing in them is dated after the cutoff. The three-year statements in the two annual reports agree on every overlapping figure tested, and the three 2026 quarters add to the nine-month revenue printed in the latest report.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_orn-20241231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 72–74; 10-K_2025-12-31_orn-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 71–74; 10-Q_2026-03-31_orn-20260331x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_orn-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-13

Debt sits with one borrower and consists of a secured bank facility led by UMB Bank, a subordinated seller note, and lessor-financed equipment and sale-leaseback obligations. The documents show no bonds, indenture or co-issuer, so there is no second issuer perimeter to reconcile. Guarantors are described as every domestic subsidiary and are not named.

Reported liquidity and debt figures can be taken as stated, and they tie out. Borrowings under the UMB facility were USD 83.9 million, availability under the revolver was about USD 28.0 million, and the two maintenance covenants are a fixed charge coverage floor of 1.20x and a senior leverage cap of 3.00x, with compliance stated at 2026-09-30. The debt table, the balance sheet and the quarterly narrative agree exactly.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-04

Four things cannot be established. Covenant headroom needs the executed credit agreement's definitions and the ratios the company reports, and neither is in the documents. The repayment profile of the term loans is not disclosed beyond the December 2030 maturity, so a maturity wall by year is incomplete. Last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA on the company definition needs a full-year 2025 reconciliation, and no document holds one. Surety capacity was last stated at the end of 2024, at least USD 1.1 billion with about USD 588 million bonded.

The sources give three different cash prices for the February 2026 acquisition of J.E. McAmis: USD 50.0 million in the 2025 annual report, USD 46.0 million in the first-quarter report and USD 44.9 million in the later two reports, all subject to adjustment. Preliminary goodwill moved from USD 32,742 thousand to USD 45,076 thousand across the same reports. The latest report governs current values and the accounting is still preliminary, so figures drawn from it can move.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_orn-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_orn-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-Q_2026-03-31_orn-20260331x10q.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_orn-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-09

Two definition differences matter when figures are compared. Total debt is USD 110,180 thousand gross in the debt note but USD 108,768 thousand after deferred issuance costs, which the release rounds to USD 109 million. The depreciation and amortisation add-back in the adjusted EBITDA reconciliation is USD 20,264 thousand against USD 15,137 thousand on the cash flow statement, and the USD 5,127 thousand difference is the amortisation of finance lease assets.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 14; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_orn-ex99d1.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-05
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest argument that the set is ready without qualification is its recency and internal consistency: it runs to 2026-09-30, every tie-out performed agrees exactly, and compliance with all covenants is stated at each of the last four reporting dates. That is enough for a reader who needs only reported figures. It is not enough for covenant headroom, a full maturity wall or last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA. The view would move to ready if the executed credit agreement with the latest reported ratios, the term loan repayment schedule and the full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA reconciliation were added.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_orn-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-Q_2026-03-31_orn-20260331x10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_orn-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation CALC-01
### Limitations
Covenant definitions, adjustments, step-downs and the ratios the company reports are not in the documents, so no headroom is measured.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 15
Purchase accounting for the acquisition is preliminary and changed between each of the three quarterly reports since closing, so values taken from it are not final.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation CALC-09
Adjusted EBITDA and guidance are company measures taken from earnings releases and are not audited.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-27_orn-ex99d1.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9
No credit rating, market price, peer set, portfolio or research question was supplied, so work that needs them is outside this snapshot.

## Request

Financial foundation for Orion Group Holdings Inc (issuer id orn-1402829), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the issuer's own consolidated statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and cover from FY2023 to the nine months to 2026-09-30, built from the eight issuer filings and releases the run supplies. It states facts and calculations, not a credit recommendation.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Debt rose from USD 7,874 thousand at the 2025 year-end to USD 108,768 thousand at 2026-09-30, lifting total debt to last-twelve-month EBITDA from 0.23x to 3.13x, and cash interest cover of 4.10x still reflects interest paid before most of that debt was drawn.

The increase paid for the February 2026 acquisition of J.E. McAmis, which accounts for USD 52,234 thousand of the USD 96,811 thousand rise in net debt, and for cash absorbed by operations: nine-month operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 10,722 thousand and capital expenditure was USD 28,109 thousand. The ratios flatter leverage because finance lease liabilities of USD 16,754 thousand sit outside debt while their costs sit outside EBITDA; counting them would put total debt to EBITDA at 3.62x.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-19; calculation CALC-20; calculation CALC-21
### Key findings

Total debt to reported EBITDA moved from 2.07x at the 2023 year-end to 0.23x at the 2025 year-end as the older term loan was repaid and cash was spent down, and then to 3.13x at 2026-09-30; net of cash it was 0.18x at the 2025 year-end, 1.72x pro forma for the acquisition of 2026-02-03, and 2.97x at 2026-09-30. The UMB bank facility entered in December 2025 supplies USD 83,926 thousand of the debt, the seller note USD 10,388 thousand and lessor-financed and sale-leaseback obligations USD 15,866 thousand, less USD 1,412 thousand of issuance costs.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_orn-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-16; calculation CALC-17; calculation CALC-19

Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 10,722 thousand in the nine months of 2026 against an inflow of USD 14,260 thousand a year earlier, because contract assets absorbed USD 52,029 thousand as work ran ahead of billing and payables and contract liabilities also fell, only partly offset by a USD 32,638 thousand release of receivables. Capital expenditure of USD 28,109 thousand and the acquisition outflow of USD 42,871 thousand took investing outflow to USD 70,213 thousand, and a financing inflow of USD 83,321 thousand funded the gap.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; calculation CALC-08

Reported EBITDA for the nine months of 2026 was USD 27,063 thousand against USD 26,381 thousand a year earlier, and issuer-adjusted EBITDA was USD 34,527 thousand against USD 32,276 thousand; add-backs of USD 7,464 thousand, mostly non-cash share-based compensation, lift reported EBITDA by 27.58%. The second quarter of 2026 was the weak point, with EBITDA of USD 5,782 thousand against USD 8,687 thousand a year earlier and a net loss of USD 4,145 thousand, after which the third quarter rebounded to EBITDA of USD 15,615 thousand.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-07-28_orn-20260728xex99d1.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_orn-ex99d1.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_orn-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation CALC-22; calculation CALC-26

Last-twelve-month cash interest of USD 8,466 thousand gives cover of 4.10x, but it predates most of the new borrowing: reported interest expense in the third quarter of 2026 alone was USD 2,950 thousand against USD 2,120 thousand a year earlier, so cover will fall as the larger debt is carried for a full year.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation CALC-07

Unrestricted cash was USD 5,671 thousand at 2026-09-30 and has ranged from USD 1,588 thousand to USD 6,254 thousand since the 2025 year-end, so the revolver is the working liquidity: availability was about USD 28.0 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 60.0 million at the 2025 year-end, before the facility was drawn to fund the acquisition and working capital.

The statements tie: each balance sheet balances, each cash flow statement adds to its net change and rolls from opening to closing cash, and the issuer's own EBITDA reconciliations add up in every period. Fiscal-year EBITDA is calculated because the issuer states none, the annual and 2026 segment operating income sit on different bases, and the three quarters add to the nine-month revenue and EBITDA exactly.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_orn-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 71, 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 5; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_orn-ex99d1.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 9; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-25; calculation CALC-26
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against reading 3.13x as stretched is that cash interest cover is 4.10x, about USD 28.0 million of revolver availability remains, backlog is USD 645 million, and the company guides full-year adjusted EBITDA to USD 50 million to USD 54 million against USD 34,527 thousand earned in nine months, which would lower leverage if delivered. The view would improve if the fourth quarter delivered that guided EBITDA with working capital reversing, and would worsen if a quarter like the second quarter of 2026 recurred while the facility stays fully drawn.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-27_orn-ex99d1.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_orn-ex99d1.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-15
### Limitations

Fiscal-year EBITDA is calculated from the statements and does not net interest income, so it can differ slightly from the issuer definition used for the 2025 and 2026 interim periods, and the last-twelve-month figures inherit that mix.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_orn-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 72
The acquired businesses contribute EBITDA only from 2026-02-03 and their stand-alone EBITDA is not stated, so last-twelve-month leverage is higher than a full-year pro forma figure would be.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8
No repayment schedule by year is disclosed for the term loans, so no maturity wall is drawn and contractual principal is not stated.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15
Interim statements are unaudited and no discrete third-quarter cash flow is printed, so cash flow metrics use year-to-date figures.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5

## Gaps

Every gap below was searched for in all eight documents, using the item's own words and synonyms, before it was recorded; each cell marked not supplied in the tables above is explained by one of these lines.

- The repayment schedule of the acquisition term loan, the equipment term loan and the lessor-financed obligations by year is not disclosed, so the maturity chart, the contractual principal and the reconciling items for 2026-09-30 are not supplied; this restricts the maturity wall and any refinancing view. Severity: High. Action: obtain the amortisation schedule of the credit agreement.

- Full-year 2025 issuer-adjusted EBITDA is not stated in any document, so adjusted EBITDA leverage and cover are not calculable for the fiscal years or for any last-twelve-month period, and the adjusted EBITDA row is empty for fiscal years. Severity: High. Action: obtain the fourth-quarter 2025 earnings release.

- Stand-alone EBITDA of the acquired businesses is not stated, so last-twelve-month leverage counts the acquisition debt in full but the acquired earnings only from 2026-02-03 and no pro forma full-year EBITDA can be given. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the acquisition presentation or the purchase agreement schedules.

- Interest income for FY2025 is not stated separately because the annual report includes it in other income, so fiscal-year EBITDA uses gross interest expense while the interim figures use the issuer's net interest; the effect on the last-twelve-month figures cannot be sized. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the interest income detail for FY2025.

- The legal rank of the lessor-financed construction obligations and the land sale-leaseback financing, together USD 15,866 thousand, is not stated, so they are left out of the debt stack and of cumulative leverage. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the lease and financing agreements.

- The principal part of each seller note instalment is not stated beyond five equal annual instalments of principal and interest, so the note's principal by year is not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the note.
- Guarantor subsidiaries are described by class and not named, and the subsidiary list exhibit is not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the subsidiary list.

- Revolver availability at 2023-12-31 is not in the documents, and the FY2023 annual report is not supplied, so undrawn committed facilities are not supplied for that date. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the FY2023 annual report.
- The undrawn part of the equipment term loan commitment is not stated as available, so it is excluded from undrawn committed facilities. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the credit agreement.

- Cells shown as not supplied in the statement tables are lines the source prints as a dash or does not present in that report, for example amortization of intangible assets within selling, general and administrative expenses after the first quarter of 2026, the impairment loss, the loss on extinguishment of debt and the term loan lines, and deferred tax lines combined into other lines in the 2026 balance sheets. Severity: Low. Action: none needed; no figure is lost.
- The FY2022 statements in the FY2024 annual report are not tabulated and the fiscal years shown start with FY2023. Severity: Low. Action: extend the period set if earlier history is needed.

- The three quarters of 2026 add to the nine-month segment revenue and segment operating income with rounding differences of 1 thousand, and the annual and 2026 segment operating income are on different bases, so no segment series is joined across them. Severity: Low. Action: none needed.

- Secured status and ranking of the UMB loans against other secured claims are stated only as security over substantially all assets, so intercreditor ranking is not established. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the credit agreement and any intercreditor terms.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Orion's creditors depend on a fixed-price, project-based contractor whose cash flow follows backlog conversion and working-capital timing, and the debt-funded 2026 acquisition of J.E. McAmis has raised the cost of an execution miss while the documents name no controlling owner or sponsor.

Marine was 63.93% of FY2025 revenue and Concrete 36.07%, but Concrete drove the 2026 growth and carries 42.08% of nine-month 2026 revenue, so credit outcomes now lean on a data-center-led concrete business alongside Navy-linked marine projects. Board independence and shareholder concentration are not established because the proxy statement is not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_orn-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 4–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03
### Key findings

The mix is moving toward concrete, which raises dependence on private demand. Concrete revenue rose 36.76% to USD 292,166 thousand in the nine months of 2026 while marine revenue fell 0.80% to USD 402,165 thousand, and private companies supplied 48.08% of nine-month revenue against 45.29% a year earlier; a slowdown in data-center or commercial building would reach the segment now doing most of the growth first.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-K_2025-12-31_orn-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-04

Revenue quality is that of a competitive fixed-price bidder, so execution and working capital, not contracted cash flow, drive repayment capacity. Most revenue comes from fixed-price contracts awarded by competitive bidding, contract assets rose by USD 53,122 thousand in nine months to USD 84,205 thousand, and claims and unapproved change orders in contract balances reached USD 17.5 million against USD 7.1 million at the 2025 year-end; remaining performance obligations of USD 645 million convert over about 18 to 24 months in marine and six to twelve months in concrete.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 12, 26; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_orn-ex99d1.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-12

Navy and joint-venture concentration is falling but still material. The U.S. Navy was 14% of FY2025 contract revenue against 25% in FY2024, and revenue from the Pearl Harbor dry dock subcontract fell to USD 47.4 million in nine months from USD 100.4 million, so replacement work matters; positions on a USD 9 billion Navy contract vehicle and a USD 700 million waterfront vehicle widen access but do not guarantee task orders.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_orn-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_orn-ex99d1.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-13

The February 2026 acquisition added marine capacity but also claims that behave like debt. Beyond the bank borrowings and the USD 12.0 million subordinated seller note, contingent payments were carried at USD 16,267 thousand at 2026-09-30, goodwill of USD 45,076 thousand equals 26.03% of equity, and measurement-period adjustments have already added about USD 12.3 million to goodwill, so the value paid is not yet fixed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 7–10, 13, 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_orn-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-08

Control and governance cannot be assessed beyond board composition. The run names no sponsor, a dispersed base of holders of record including beneficial holders is reported, no controlling shareholder is stated, and vessel-owning entities must meet United States citizenship ownership rules, but ownership concentration, board independence and compensation sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, and the chief financial officer and one director joined in 2025 while executive employment agreements were amended in September 2026 and a new chief financial officer agreement was signed in October 2026.

Financial policy was supportive of creditors until the 2026 acquisition. The 2024 equity offering raised about USD 26.4 million of net proceeds that were used partly to repay bank debt, no dividend or repurchase appears in any cash flow statement or share record, and the 2025 refinancing replaced a facility that carried a 10.70% weighted average rate with a bank facility priced at 2.50% to 3.00% over the reference rate; the 2026 acquisition then reversed the deleveraging with borrowing.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is the order book and end markets: backlog was USD 645 million at 2026-09-30, third-quarter awards were USD 179 million, the company reports GAAP net income of USD 5,473 thousand for the quarter, and no sponsor or shareholder has extracted cash. The view would soften if backlog conversion shows contract assets reversing and claims settling at their booked value, and would harden if a marine project overrun, a data-center slowdown or an unfavourable measurement-period change to the contingent payments emerged.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 12, 27; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_orn-ex99d1.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation CALC-05
### Limitations

- Control and board independence are not established, so the conclusion that no controlling owner or sponsor stands behind the credit would change if a holder of a large stake appears in the proxy statement.
- Stand-alone results of the acquired businesses are not stated, so the contribution of the acquisition to marine revenue and margin cannot be separated from organic change.
- Surety capacity is not quantified after 2024-12-31, so the conclusion that bonding does not limit growth rests on management's qualitative statement.
- Segment operating income appears on two bases, so any margin conclusion by segment holds only on the 2026 basis.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

On 2026-02-03 Orion completed the purchase of J.E. McAmis, Inc. and JEM Marine Leasing, LLC, paying cash of USD 44.907 million at the latest measurement, issuing a USD 12.0 million unsecured subordinated 6.0% five-year note payable in five equal annual instalments, issuing 182,392 shares and agreeing contingent payments on project profit; about USD 46.9 million of UMB borrowings funded the cash and related expenses. The new debt issued in the period is bank debt under the December 2025 UMB credit agreement, with USD 83,926 thousand drawn across the revolver and the two term loans at 2026-09-30, the seller note, and lessor-financed obligations; no bonds or notes were issued to investors, and two interest rate swaps fix part of the floating cost.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Orion presents an adequate but thinly protected credit: a USD 645 million backlog supports revenue, but negative cash conversion, a debt step-up to 3.13x EBITDA and unproven covenant headroom leave repayment dependent on working capital reversing in the fourth quarter.

Cash and revolver availability of USD 33,671 thousand compare with a nine-month free cash outflow of USD 38,831 thousand, so liquidity is adequate only if the USD 53,122 thousand build in contract assets unwinds; guidance of USD 50 million to USD 54 million of adjusted EBITDA implies a fourth quarter close to the third. The company states covenant compliance, but headroom cannot be computed because the executed agreement and the reported ratios are not supplied.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 14, 30; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_orn-ex99d1.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 11; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-09
### Key findings

Liquidity is adequate only on the assumption that working capital reverses. Unrestricted cash was USD 5,671 thousand and revolver availability about USD 28.0 million at 2026-09-30, together USD 33,671 thousand, which is 0.87x of the nine-month free cash outflow of USD 38,831 thousand, and the revolver is 48.33% drawn before letters of credit; management states that liquidity is adequate for at least the next twelve months.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 14, 30; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-10

Cash conversion has broken down while margins are thin. Last-twelve-month operating cash flow was USD 3,084 thousand against EBITDA of USD 34,714 thousand, a conversion of 8.88% against 82.47% in FY2025, as contract assets rose to 9.08% of last-twelve-month revenue from 3.65% at the 2025 year-end; EBITDA was only 3.74% of last-twelve-month revenue, so a small cost overrun on fixed-price work removes a large share of earnings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 5; calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-06

Leverage has stepped up and the ratio flatters. Total debt was 3.13x last-twelve-month EBITDA and 2.97x net of cash at 2026-09-30, rising to 3.62x if finance lease liabilities are counted as debt, and cash interest cover of 4.10x predates most of the new borrowing; swaps fix the rate on an amount equal to the USD 40,000 thousand acquisition term loan, while the revolver and equipment loan float at a weighted average rate of 6.2%, 4.50 percentage points below the 2025 weighted rate on the facility it replaced.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16, 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_orn-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 88; calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-08

Refinancing risk sits in liquidity, not in a maturity wall, but the wall is not fully visible. The bank facility matures in December 2030 and no bonds are outstanding, so repayment depends on the revolver and on cash generation rather than on market access; the term loan repayment schedule is not disclosed, the secured lenders hold substantially all assets, and the seller note and contingent payments add claims that are paid from the same cash.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16; 10-K_2025-12-31_orn-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 87–89

Business risk is project execution on fixed-price work, increasingly in concrete. Most revenue is fixed-price and competitively bid, concrete carries 42.08% of nine-month revenue after growing 36.76%, and Navy-linked marine work is falling, so earnings now lean on private data-center and commercial demand; the USD 645 million backlog and positions on large Navy contract vehicles give visibility but not contracted margin.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12, 26–27; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_orn-ex99d1.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

Governance and financial policy cannot be rated, and the observable record is mixed. No sponsor or controlling holder is stated, no dividend or repurchase is shown, and equity raised in 2024 repaid debt, but the 2026 acquisition was funded with debt and contingent payments of USD 16,267 thousand, and ownership, independence and compensation sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_orn-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 60–61, 94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 7–10, 13, 16

The primary downside path starts with a marine project overrun or an unapproved change order that stays in contract assets. Claims and unapproved change orders were USD 17.5 million in the balances, so a settlement below book value cuts earnings and holds billed cash back, availability of USD 28.0 million is drawn to cover payroll and equipment, interest rises on the floating part of the debt, and fixed charge coverage and senior leverage covenants of 1.20x and 3.00x then bind; the observable triggers are availability, contract assets and the next quarter's operating cash flow.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 14–15; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-06
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is guidance and order intake: full-year adjusted EBITDA is guided to USD 50 million to USD 54 million, which implies fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 15,473 thousand to USD 19,473 thousand against USD 17,917 thousand in the third quarter, and at that level the 2026-09-30 debt would be 2.01x to 2.18x adjusted EBITDA. Backlog of USD 645 million, third-quarter awards of USD 179 million and management's statement of adequate liquidity for twelve months support the same reading. The view would improve if the fourth quarter shows contract assets and receivables turning to cash and availability rising, and would worsen if the next report shows a further operating cash outflow, a guidance cut like the one in July, or a covenant amendment.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-27_orn-ex99d1.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 11; EX-99.1_2026-07-28_orn-20260728xex99d1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 30; calculation CALC-09; calculation CALC-11
### Limitations
- No credit rating, market price or peer data is supplied, so the view that leverage is elevated is not benchmarked and could be softer against the sector.
- The executed credit agreement is not supplied, so the conclusion that liquidity is adequate cannot be tested against covenant limits and any step-downs.
- Seasonality of working capital is not stated, so the expectation that contract assets unwind in the fourth quarter rests on guidance rather than on a pattern.
- The downside path is qualitative because the documents give no stress parameters, so no stressed leverage or liquidity figure is stated.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength: order book and end-market demand. Backlog stood at USD 645 million and third-quarter awards were USD 179 million, concrete revenue grew 36.76% in nine months on data-center and commercial demand, and the company holds positions on two large Navy contract vehicles; this supports revenue visibility over 6 to 24 months, though not margin.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 12, 27; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_orn-ex99d1.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation CALC-12

Strength: cheaper and simpler funding after the refinancing. The 2025 refinancing replaced a facility that cost 10.70% with a bank facility at a weighted average rate of 6.2%, no bonds are outstanding, and last-twelve-month cash interest cover is 4.10x; lower interest eases debt service while the business rebuilds cash flow.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_orn-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 87–88; 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; Financial foundation (CP-1)
Strength: no evidence of cash leaving for owners. No dividend or repurchase appears and equity raised in 2024 repaid debt, so cash stays available to creditors.

Weakness: negative cash conversion. Nine-month operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 10,722 thousand and capital expenditure USD 28,109 thousand, so free cash flow was negative USD 38,831 thousand and the revolver funds the gap; repayment depends on working capital reversing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-04

Weakness: leverage and contingent claims after a debt-funded acquisition. Total debt is 3.13x EBITDA, the seller note and contingent payments rank as further claims, and goodwill is large against equity; an execution miss lands on a more leveraged balance sheet.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 7–10; calculation CALC-07

Weakness: thin fixed-price margins and concentration. EBITDA is 3.74% of last-twelve-month revenue, most work is fixed-price, and earnings depend on a few large projects, Texas-centred concrete and private demand.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12, 26; calculation CALC-05

Weakness: unknown covenant headroom and debt amortisation. Covenants of 1.20x fixed charge coverage and 3.00x senior leverage are stated with compliance, but the reported ratios, definitions and the term loan schedule are not supplied, so headroom and the maturity wall are not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_orn-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; Source readiness (CP-0)
